title: Water Treatment & Filtration
painPoint: Water treatment and filtration systems rely on NdFeB magnets for magnetic separation of contaminants, scale prevention, and fluid purification. However, continuous exposure to aqueous environments subjects magnets to corrosive degradation, with standard nickel-copper-nickel coatings failing within months in chlorinated and saline process water. High-flow magnetic filter assemblies experience thermal stress when handling heated effluent streams, pushing N48 and N50 grades toward irreversible demagnetization above 80 degrees C. Engineers struggle to maintain field intensities above 10,000 gauss across large-diameter filter housings while ensuring long-term magnetic stability in systems operating 24/7 without maintenance access.
